# Talks & Service

## Scholarship, Leadership, and Academic Engagement

My academic work extends beyond teaching and research to include conference presentations, scholarly service, professional leadership, and community engagement.

I view these activities as opportunities to contribute to academic communities, support emerging scholars, share research with broader audiences, and help connect data, technology, education, and practice.

---

## Selected Presentations

### Technology Integration for Diverse Learners

**Itauma, I. (2024).**  
*Technology Integration for Diverse Learners: Enhancing Engagement and Accessibility.*

Regional Center for Educational Planning (RCEP) UNESCO Symposium.

This presentation focused on the role of technology in creating more inclusive, accessible, and engaging learning environments.

---

### Factors Predicting Mathematics and Science Motivation

**Itauma, I., Robertson, A., Fuda-Daddio, J., & Komaroff, E. (2024).**  
*Factors Predicting Mathematics and Science Motivation among Minority Female High School Students.*

American Educational Research Association Annual Meeting, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

This research examined factors associated with STEM motivation among minority female high school students and reflects my broader interest in education, student success, and STEM participation.

## Doctoral Scholar Spotlight

### Dr. Shemika S. Miller

**Dissertation:** *A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Impact of Leader-Member Exchange (LMX) Quality on Employee Turnover Intentions*

Dr. Shemika S. Miller completed her doctoral dissertation at Northwood University in 2024.

I had the privilege of serving as her dissertation chair and supporting her through the research process, including methodological development, quantitative synthesis, interpretation of findings, and successful completion of the dissertation.

Her work represents the type of doctoral scholarship I aim to encourage: theoretically grounded, methodologically rigorous, evidence-based, and relevant to both scholarship and organizational practice.

> **Miller, S. S. (2024).** *A systematic review and meta-analysis of the impact of leader-member exchange (LMX) quality on employee turnover intentions* [Doctoral dissertation, Northwood University].

[View the Dissertation on ProQuest](https://www.proquest.com/openview/9ea639844d6013c44f21d91ce9facba6/1?pq-origsite=gscholar&cbl=18750&diss=y)
